pr_title: roachprod: support for dynamic admin url port
pr_body:
In order to support multiple tenants on the same host, a unique, custom port can be assigned for DefaultAdminUIPort. This breaks because the port is hard-coded in prometheus config for scraping.

The change is to have a http server running in prometheus server that can dynamically update the configuration when a new cluster is brought up. More details of the solution is explained in the page - https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~7120207825326fb5e546c194029506f2c5335e/pages/3458531376/Dynamic+Scrape+Configs+on+Prometheus+for+Roachprod

Fixes: #117125
Epic: none

Thanks for your work so far! I'll leave some high level comments, curious what others think of the approach.

I'm of the opinion that the main goal of this HTTP service is to be as simple as possible. By "simple", I mean having the least amount of internal logic. Our original / ideal design was for these configuration files to be automatically synchronized based on changes in a storage bucket somewhere. Given we can't have that, the next best thing is a caller (`roachprod`) telling the service exactly what to do ("create file foo.txt with contents `xyz`").

I want us to rarely (never) need to redeploy this service: if the service has a more sophisticated API (i.e., request body is cluster ID and labels, mapping of ports), then any change on that API will require changes in this service (which will be manual and painful). Not to mention issues of backwards-compatibility.

With a lower level API (two endpoints: create file, and delete file), this is much less likely to happen. 

``` console
# on grafana server
$ ./start-server <path-to-directory-being-watched-by-prometheus>
```

roachprod would run the equivalent of

```console
$ cat body.json
{"path": "mycluster.json", "data": "{prometheus-config}"}

$ curl -XPOST "/create" -d @body.json <service-url>
````

when a cluster is created.

With an approach like this, the vast majority of changes to evolve this setup will come from roachprod, not this service. In other words, it will minimize the maintenance work we will need to do (which again will be manual and not fun).

Thoughts?

I agree with the point around (re)deployment. Thanks @renatolabs for reviewing the changes!

I initially took a more controlled approach to have more control on how the file is created as this API will be accessible for all. The same was mentioned in the document.
I am fine with this approach if all agrees to this.

Also, regarding the directory path as input - this makes the API layer specific to the cluster config use case. As you can see the code, the knowledge of the directory is only in the intanceconfigs handlers layer. I will try to change the code so that each handler can register its flags.
I made the changes to have a way to register flags for the handlers and changed the APIs to just take the file content as input. I will update the doc accordingly.

issue_context.title: roachtest: using custom AdminUIPort breaks automated prometheus scraping
issue_context.body:
Per [1], in order to support multiple tenants on the same host, a unique, custom SQLPort is assigned (instead of `DefaultSQLPort`), similarly for `DefaultAdminUIPort`. The latter breaks current integration with Prometheus' service discovery which is configured to scrape on `DefaultAdminUIPort` (26258). Per [2], some tests revert to it via an explicit call to `SetDefaultAdminUIPort`. Otherwise, a custom AdminUIPort is used, in which case the metrics no longer show up in Grafana. Thus, a number of roachtest failures are now without metrics; e.g., grafana link in [3] yields no data.

[1] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/111052
[2] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/114097
[3] https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/116992

Jira issue: CRDB-34993

review_comments:
general naming remark, since the package is called `instanceconfigs`, we can drop it from the names to help simplify them a bit.

i.e `func getInstanceConfigDir()` -> `getDir`
Hmm, I'm not entirely sure if we want to use `zap logger` for unit tests. But maybe it's okay, let me think about it.
Thanks! have not put much thought around this. As long as the interface is satisfied, we can decide on any logger.

Why do we need to add the clusterID this way when it should already be part of the endpoint?

i.e. before calling `req.SetPathValue(ClusterIDParam, clusterName)` the URL is: `DELETE URL:/instance-configs/test-cluster_1712091001500145000` 

Shouldn't it be able to just parse that instead of looking into `PathValue`.
When you are using a n actual http call, the value is  by default available as `PathValue`. But, in this case, the path value does not get set. So, I had to do this hack in the test.
